newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's PTS telecom approves share issues.
newsitem.headline: Russia's PTS telecom approves share issues.

text.p: Russia's St Petersburg Telephone (PTS) approved issuing 44.1 million preferred shares and 2.5 million ordinary shares this year at the annual meeting on Friday, the company's director for economy and finance said.
Shareholders will have priority rights to the new issues, Natalya Shevchuk told Reuters.
Shevchuk said AO Peterburgskaya Telefonaya Set expected the new issues would raise $40 million which the company intended to use for modernisation.
The meeting approved dividends on preferred PTS shares of 170 roubles per 1,000 rouble nominal share after 3,880 per 50 rouble nominal in the previous year.
Ordinary dividends of 16 roubles per 1,000 nominal, after nothing last year, were also approved.
Charter capital was revalued in 1996 and rose to 466.46 billion roubles from 777.46 million.
PTS had 382.29 million ordinary shares and 84.19 million preferred shares as of January 17, CentreInvest Securities said.
Its net profit rose to 198.14 billion roubles in 1996 from 150.8 billion in 1995 on sales of 875.5 billion and 513.7 billion roubles.
Two representatives of Crawford Holding were among nine new directors elected.

Major shareholders include Russian holding company Svyazinvest with 41.8 percent of shares and Cyprus-registered Crawford Holdings Ltd and Knightsbridge Finance with 12.4 and 7.5 percent respectively. CS First Boston owns 6.31.
PTS shares had fallen to $1.51 at 1330 GMT on the Russian Trading System from $1.51 on Thursday, though only a handful of deals had been reported over the two days.
